walkthroughs.body_html:
Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: The Existence of God — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: The Existence of God brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: The Existence of God.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Paley's watchmaker analogy supports which argument for God's existence?
options: The design (teleological) argument
The cosmological argument
The ontological argument
The moral argument

mcqs.q: Aquinas's First Cause argument is a version of which argument?
options: The cosmological argument
The design argument
The ontological argument
The argument from religious experience

mcqs.q: The problem of evil challenges which two attributes of God?
options: Omnipotence and omnibenevolence
Transcendence and immanence
Eternity and immutability
Unity and simplicity

mcqs.q: Who defined God as 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived'?
options: Anselm
Paley
Darwin
Dawkins

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological argument actually claim?
options: The cosmological argument claims the universe is itself God.
That everything that exists has a cause, an infinite regress of causes is impossible, so there must be an uncaused First Cause, which Aquinas identified as God.
An agnostic is someone who attends church without enjoying it.
The cosmological argument says God exists because the Bible says so.

mcqs.q: Does Paley's design argument prove God's existence with certainty?
options: The cosmological argument claims the universe is itself God.
No — it is an inductive argument claiming design is the best explanation of order in nature; critics like Hume, and Darwin's evolution, offer alternative explanations, so it is probable at best.
Paley's watch analogy gives conclusive proof that God exists.
Paley argued that watches occur naturally without any maker.

mcqs.q: Is an agnostic the same as an atheist?
options: Agnostics and atheists both assert that God definitely does not exist.
An agnostic is someone who attends church without enjoying it.
Paley argued that watches occur naturally without any maker.
No — an atheist believes there is no God, while an agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known or proven either way.
